title: Getting started
Start here in 5 minutes
body:
Your first result is a catalogue containing The Matrix. You need an Ether development server you control, its admin token, and the Ether CLI from this checkout. No provider account or media download is needed. The sample describes a movie; playback still needs an owner-configured playable source.

## 1. Create a plugin (one minute)
From the repository root, build the CLI once if it is not already on your PATH:

```sh
CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o ./ether ./cmd/ether
./ether plugin new catalogue --lang ts ./my-first-plugin
```

Open `my-first-plugin/src/index.ts` and find the `/catalog/` branch. It returns a real Stremio `metas` entry with an IMDb ID, type and name. The manifest declares the matching `featured` catalogue and a list source named Featured picks. Change the reverse-DNS plugin ID in the manifest before distributing your own project.

## 2. Get a green check (one minute)

```sh
./ether plugin check ./my-first-plugin
./ether plugin test ./my-first-plugin
```

Expect `PASS`. Errors name the field or route to fix and link to its reference topic. For an agent, use `./ether plugin check --json ./my-first-plugin`. All generated templates work without npm dependencies. The check is offline; your local server is used only in the next step.

## 3. Install and keep the loop open (one minute)
Set `ETHER_TOKEN` in your shell to your local server's admin token, then run:

```sh
./ether plugin dev ./my-first-plugin --server http://localhost:32400
```

Use your development server's actual port if it differs. Expect `Reloaded community.example.myfirstplugin` followed by `Watching`. The watcher checks conformance before installing each saved change and prints plugin logs. If a save fails, fix the reported field and save again; the watcher stays open. Ctrl-C stops it. A 401/403 means the token or grants need attention; a connection error means the server address or process needs attention.

## 4. See your result (one minute)
In that server's console, open Plugins and enable your plugin after reviewing its permissions. Open Collections → New collection. In Sources, choose Featured picks from your plugin, replacing the default catalogue source if present. Keep the media type Movies. The collection preview resolves the sample's IMDb ID to The Matrix in your Ether catalogue. If it is missing, confirm the plugin is enabled and that your development catalogue contains that title; the sample does not populate Ether's TMDB catalogue itself.

For an immediate plugin-owned page without catalogue matching, scaffold `extension` instead of `catalogue`, install it with the same dev command, then open its Language overview page from the plugin. Its ViewSpec displays the sample active language, `en`.

## 5. Make it yours and share it (one minute)
Edit the catalogue response, save, and re-open the collection preview. Keep IDs stable and page larger results. Put configuration in `settings.schema.json`, labels in `i18n/en.json`, and secrets in sealed settings rather than source. When the result looks right:

```sh
./ether plugin pack -o ./my-first-plugin.etherpkg ./my-first-plugin
./ether plugin check ./my-first-plugin.etherpkg
```

Upload that package through Plugins → Add plugin on another development server. See [the authoring recipes](/plugins/reference/agent-recipes) for ten directions to take next, [Capabilities](/plugins/reference/capabilities) for route shapes, and [Testing](/plugins/reference/testing) for the limits of offline checks.

title: Recipes for humans and coding agents
body: Start with one useful response, then build the next thing you want to use. The guide below covers ten plugin types, exact CLI commands, manifest decisions, host-service permissions, and common repairs. Use the header’s Copy for your AI assistant button to copy all chapters and generated contracts, or give your agent `/ether/plugins/reference/llms.txt` on this server. Hosted code has no Node filesystem or npm resolution; use the shipped host-service contracts and bundle imports.

title: Manifest
body:
Every package has `manifest.json`. `id`, `version`, and `name` are required. The native `ether` block requires protocol, kind, and runtime. A manifest without that block is a plain Stremio add-on. Keep reverse-DNS identity stable and increase SemVer for updates.

```json
{"id":"org.example.hello","name":"Hello","version":"0.1.0","ether":{"protocol":1,"kind":"extension","runtime":{"kind":"hosted","entry":"plugin.js"}}}
```

## Reading the generated fields
The schema table lists required fields **within their parent object**, constraints, enum values, and explicitly declared defaults. An optional parent need not be present. Absence of a schema default does not imply zero is the runtime default: consult the Go type comments and validator below. Go field tables describe serialization, not validation requiredness. `omitempty` never proves that a field is optional for your chosen capability.

Network permissions, contribution metadata, settings references, schedules, and runtime entry points are validated together. For `ether.schedule`, the first run happens right after install (within one scheduler tick once enabled). Later runs resume from the last dispatch plus `every` across server restarts, including failed attempts; overdue entries run on the next tick. Due entries run sequentially through the existing plugin call path, including `/ether/job/` deadlines. Errors identify the field to fix. See [Capabilities](/plugins/reference/capabilities), [Settings](/plugins/reference/settings), and [Publishing](/plugins/reference/publishing).

title: Capabilities & contribution routes
body:
Capabilities describe what a plugin does; permissions describe which host data it can use. Declare only the capabilities you implement. Required contribution metadata depends on the capability and plugin kind; the generated validator below enumerates all combinations and errors.

| Capability | Entry point or contribution |
|---|---|
| stream_source | Stremio `/stream/{type}/{id}.json`; lazy streams open through `/ether/open/{id}` |
| debrid_provider | `/ether/debrid/check`, `find`, `acquire`, `link`, `remove`, `account` |
| debrid_cache_hints | `POST /ether/debrid/hints` on a viewer's Play: which listed torrents a debrid service holds |
| list_source | `contributes.listSources`; matching Stremio catalogue |
| poster_badges | `contributes.posterBadges`; `ether.badges.set`, `clear`, `usage` |
| metadata | Stremio `/meta/{type}/{id}.json` |
| plugin_directory | Plugin directory declarations and discovery routes |
| livetv_channels | `/ether/channels.json`, `/ether/guide/{id}.json`, stream routes |
| subtitles | Stremio subtitles resource; declared languages and formats |
| markers | Declared intro, credits, recap or preview marker kinds |
| notify | Notification metadata; send and send-test handlers |
| events | Event subscriptions (`POST /ether/event`) and custom published events (`contributes.events.publish`, `ether.events.publish`) |
| flow_actions | Declared Flow actions (`contributes.flowActions`) invoked via `POST /ether/v1/flow-actions/{key}` with `X-Ether-Idempotency-Key` |
| ranking_step | Deterministic `rank_key(candidate, config)` |
| rule_condition | Deterministic `cond_match(candidate, operator, value)` |
| tools | Declared tool input schema and tool handlers |
| ui | Pages, slots, commands, ViewSpec views and actions |
| onair_content / livetv_pack | Declared On Air segments or TV pack contributions |
| catalog_provider / kind_resolver / matcher | Content kind browse, resolve, match routes |
| frontend_adapter | Authenticated protocol adapter routes |

Reserved capability names cannot be claimed in EPP/1. Ranking and condition hot paths have only log and abort: no I/O, wall clock, or arbitrary host calls. Return a neutral result when there is no useful adjustment. Consult the generated templates and route checks for each response shape rather than inventing one.

title: Content kinds & libraries
body:
See the complete content-kind guide below. Start with a bounded browse page, stable external IDs, and a playable leaf. Use [Resolvers](/plugins/reference/resolvers) for bytes and [Folders](/plugins/reference/host-folders) for local files.

### Reporting a route failure

Return a non-2xx response with a body such as `{"error":{"code":"rate_limited","message":"The catalogue service is rate limiting requests","retryAfterSeconds":300}}`. Ether recognizes `auth`, `rate_limited`, `upstream_unavailable`, `not_found` and `invalid_settings`. Use one owner-facing sentence and omit credentials and URLs. Map upstream 401/403 to `auth` even if the route itself returns 502. Send `Retry-After` or a positive `retryAfterSeconds` when known. Return 501 if the optional changes route is unimplemented.

title: Screens and surfaces
body:
Give Vela a screen of your own (a sports desk, a news front page) or fill a host slot: a player overlay, an alert toast, a Home row or a title panel. You ship **documents**: JSON files in your package that Vela draws natively on TV, phone and web in the viewer's skin. The full contract is `docs/plugin-screens.md`; the document schema is `schemas/plugin-screen.v1.json`.

## Declare
Add the `screens` capability and `contributes.screens: [{id, title, icon, pages: {index: "screens/x.json"}, actions?}]` or `contributes.surfaces: [{id, presentation, anchor?, setting?, when?, document}]`. `when` may only name your own feeds and kinds.

## Write a document
`{schema: 1, kind: "screen", renderer: 19, params, sources, strings, tree}`. The tree is Vela's node language. `params` are typed page inputs; `sources` name data Ether resolves per viewer: `liveEvents`, `liveSchedule`, `liveEvent`, `liveTables`, `liveEntities`, `liveLeagues`, `watch`, `viewer` and `plugin`. Arguments may hold `{param.x}`, `{viewer.tz}` and, on surfaces, `{context.event}` style holes; never another source. Documents never contain URLs: write `asset:path` for package files.

## Answer a plugin source
```ts
p.onScreenSource("desk", "front", async ({ args }) => ({
  value: { lead: record("story", "s1") },
  records: [{ type: "story", id: "s1", value: { title: "…", hero: image("https://cdn.example.com/a.jpg"), url: link("https://example.com/s1") } }],
  maxAgeSec: 120, nextRefreshSec: 60,
}));
```
Wrap images (`image`, `asset`), links (`link`), records (`record`), events (`event`) and entities (`entity`). Ether signs images only on your `permissions.network` hosts and drops bare URL strings. `scope: "viewer"` sources receive the viewer like a frontend adapter call.

## Actions
Declare typed `actions` on the screen; answer `onScreenAction` with `{records?, sources?, refresh?, toast?, navigate?}`. Ether's own `ether.favorite`, `ether.reveal` and `ether.spoilerFree` need no code.

## Live
While a viewer has a page open, Ether re-reads it on live feed changes, on your `nextRefreshSec`, and when you call `ether.screens.invalidate()`. `ether.screens.putRecords([{type, id, value}])` patches records already on screen. Nobody watching costs nothing.

## Check
`ether plugin check` compiles every document exactly as install does and reports each problem by file and JSON pointer.

title: Catalogue sources
body:
A Stremio catalogue returns `{metas:[...]}` for `/catalog/{type}/{id}.json`. The catalogue ID must match `manifest.catalogs` and `ether.contributes.listSources[].catalog`. A list source can appear in collections and home rows; it is different from the signed **plugin marketplace catalogue** described in [Publishing](/plugins/reference/publishing).

```json
{"key":"weekly","label":"This week","catalog":"weekly","maxItems":50,"refresh":"1h"}
```

Keep pages bounded, handle search and pagination extras consistently, and use stable metadata IDs. Read parameters from the request; do not return an entire remote library to answer one query. For arbitrary media hierarchies use [Content kinds](/plugins/reference/kinds), whose provider sync persists items in Ether's store.

title: Resolvers & playback
body:
Resolve only when a viewer requests playback. Browse and metadata must stay cheap. A content-kind resolver returns ordered `sources`; an empty array means temporarily unavailable. File, range, download, direct, container, and release patterns have different ownership of fetching and caching; read the generated PlayableSource types and content-kind guide.

```json
{"sources":[{"id":"primary","pattern":"range","url":"https://media.example.org/track.mp3","mime":"audio/mpeg"}]}
```

Use `{secret:name}` header placeholders instead of returning raw credentials. URLs support only the documented integer placeholders. Return `unavailable` on kind items when an owner needs to see why verified bytes do not exist. Use Ether stream tickets for frontend adapters so media bypasses the plugin process. See [Kinds](/plugins/reference/kinds), [Source discovery](/plugins/reference/host-sources), and the native debrid route/error table below.

title: Notification channels
body:
`kind: "notification_channel"` with capability `notify` registers a delivery channel. This differs from `ether.notify.owner`, which posts a console notice. Declare `contributes.notification` with `sendTest: true`, supported formats, optional fields, and maximum length. Owners configure channel instances through Notifications.

```json
{"kind":"notification_channel","capabilities":["notify"],"contributes":{"notification":{"sendTest":true,"formats":["text"],"maxLength":1000}}}
```

Implement `POST /ether/notify` (the SDK notify handler). It receives the delivery request, including its test flag for a test send; return the documented NotifyResponse. See the generated router and conformance checks below. Validate channel fields and authenticate external delivery through declared network hosts and secrets. A successful connection test must mean the service accepted the request; do not report success after an upstream error. Never log tokens or signed delivery URLs. The Home Assistant example shows remote notification delivery.

title: Styles for On Air
body:
A plugin can be a channel style for On Air: idents, up-next cards, breaks and the rest of a channel's look, plus the artwork and fonts it uses. Style plugins run no code. Styles are shared this way; there is no separate pack format.

## The quickest way
Design the style in Live TV → Styles, then open its menu and choose **Export as plugin**. The download is a complete `.etherpkg` style plugin. Install it on another server from Plugins (upload, URL or Marketplace), or submit it to the Marketplace like any other plugin.

## Manifest
A style plugin uses the data runtime and contributes exactly one style:

```json
{
  "id": "community.style.neon-noir",
  "name": "Neon Noir",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "ether": {
    "protocol": 1,
    "kind": "extension",
    "summary": "Adds a channel style and its licensed artwork",
    "runtime": { "kind": "data" },
    "capabilities": ["livetv_pack"],
    "contributes": { "looks": [{ "id": "style", "file": "looks/style.json" }] }
  }
}
```

The rules Ether checks:
- `runtime.kind` is `data` with no `entry` or `module`.
- `livetv_pack` is the only capability.
- `contributes.looks` holds exactly one style.

## Files
- `looks/style.json`: the style document, the same JSON the Style editor saves (brand, roles, scenes, controls).
- `assets/<sha256>`: each Library image, video, audio file or font the style references by digest.
- `assets.json`: one entry per asset, with `digest`, `name`, `kind`, `license`, `mime`, and optional `source` and `attribution`.
- `digest`: the package digest. Export writes it; the CLI writes it for hand-built packages.

## Limits and licences
- One file may be at most 64 MB, and the whole package at most 128 MB.
- Fonts travel only with a licence that permits redistribution. Export swaps any other font for the bundled Inter and lists it in `warnings.json`.
- Installing the plugin adds the style to the owner's Styles, labelled with the plugin it came from. The style stays if the plugin is removed; delete it from Styles.

title: Settings & setup steps
Events & Flows
body:
Subscribe explicitly with capability `events` and `contributes.events.subscribe`, and handle deliveries at `POST /ether/event`. Both the 12 legacy EPP/1 event names and canonical Flows event names are supported; unknown names are rejected.

```json
{"capabilities":["events","flow_actions"],"contributes":{"events":{"subscribe":["playback.session.started"],"publish":[{"key":"scene.changed","label":"Scene changed","fields":[{"name":"scene","type":"string","label":"Scene"}]}]},"flowActions":[{"key":"set_scene","label":"Set scene","route":"/ether/v1/flow-actions/set_scene","idempotent":true,"params":[{"key":"scene","type":"string","label":"Scene","required":true}]}]}}
```

## Publishing custom events
Declare schemas under `contributes.events.publish` and emit events via `ether.events.publish(key, payload[, correlation])` (hosted) or `POST /ether/plugin-host/events/publish` (remote). Ether registers each published event as `plugin:<pluginId>/<key>`, validates payloads against the declared schema (max 64 KiB), and rate-limits publishing to 30 events/minute per plugin.

## Contributing Flow actions
Declare capability `flow_actions` and actions under `contributes.flowActions` with a route under `/ether/` and optional timeout (default 30 s, max 60 s). Ether registers each action as `plugin:<pluginId>/<key>` atomically across install, update, grant changes, and uninstall, and invokes it via `POST` with `X-Ether-Idempotency-Key` and body `{flowId, runId, nodeId, idempotencyKey, dryRun, params}`. Deduplicate side effects with `X-Ether-Idempotency-Key`, honor `dryRun`, and return `{output: {...}, branch?}`.

Keep event and action handlers bounded and idempotent. Viewer identity and secret fields are redacted per live grants. Enabled subscriptions are indexed; nobody subscribing means no plugin outbox work. See the Smart Lights example below.

title: Testing & conformance
body:
Use Studio's run and preview tools while editing. Before distributing, run the offline conformance command on an unpacked package:

```sh
ether plugin check ./my-plugin
```

The kit validates manifest fields, package references, owner-facing copy, declared routes, capability response shapes, and hot-path determinism/budgets. Content-kind checks cover pagination termination, page limits, detail round trips, declared live search, and resolver patterns. Shared kind fixtures live in `sdk/conformance/kinds`.

Mock external HTTP, store, viewer, and playback dependencies in SDK tests. Check missing grants, revoked grants, empty results, rate limits, invalid settings, and upstream failures. Offline conformance cannot prove a paid account works: after installation, run the owner's connection test with real credentials. Inspect Studio's calls and logs without exposing secrets. Package only after these checks; see [Publishing](/plugins/reference/publishing).

title: Packaging & publishing
body:
Bundle hosted SDK imports into the entry artifact. Bare package imports cannot resolve in the hosted virtual filesystem. Put the manifest, referenced settings/strings, and compiled entry into the package; do not include credentials or development caches.

```sh
ether plugin check ./my-plugin
ether plugin publish --url https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/download/v0.1.0/<id>-0.1.0.etherpkg ./my-plugin
```

Keep identity stable and increment version. New permissions require owner review; removing or retyping kind declarations can require explicit replacement approval. Test upgrades and the owner's rollback flow before release.

Ether reads the official signed marketplace (`https://github.com/braedonsaunders/ether-plugins`, served at `https://braedonsaunders.github.io/ether-plugins/index.json`) by default under Plugins → Marketplace. Upload `<id>-<version>.etherpkg` to a GitHub release, run `ether plugin publish --url <release-asset-url> ./my-plugin` to pack the archive and print a validated `plugins/<id>.yaml` entry with its SHA-256 digest, and open a pull request against `https://github.com/braedonsaunders/ether-plugins`. Marketplace CI verifies the package digest and runs `ether plugin check` before publishing the Ed25519-signed index. Owners running their own catalogue can use the template below and set `plugins.indexUrl` and `plugins.publicKey` together.

title: Examples & Studio templates
body: Copy a complete example matching your capability, then change the manifest ID before installing. Examples include hello in three languages, local folders, kind libraries, debrid, subtitles, live TV, notifications, and event-driven integrations. Generated Studio templates show raw hosted handlers; SDK examples show bundled or remote programs. All examples below are copyable and searchable.

title: Troubleshooting & errors
body:
| Symptom | Check |
|---|---|
| Manifest rejected | Field path and validator message; capability-specific metadata; unsupported names; referenced files |
| Permission denied | Manifest declaration plus current owner grant; a grant may have been revoked since startup |
| Disabled or unavailable | Plugin enabled state, required setup, injected backend availability, saved secrets |
| Network failure | Host allowlist, guarded redirects, private-address protection, body cap, upstream status |
| Folder inaccessible | Hosted runtime, owner-picked root, relative path, symlink containment, revoked grant |
| Hash too large | Use hashStart above 256 MiB; poll until terminal; retry a busy worker later |
| SDK import unresolved | Bundle imports into the hosted entry; do not expect Node resolution in QuickJS |
| Empty library | Setup completion, sync mode, page cursors, declared levels/field types, stable IDs |
| Playback unavailable | Resolver pattern, source URL, secret placeholders, item unavailable reason, viewer access |
| Remote 401 | Plugin credential or tunnel pairing; never substitute a viewer token |
| Rate limited | Honor backoff and bounded work; owner notices allow five per hour |

Generated validators, transport error mapping, and runtime fault definitions below give the exact error messages. Search a message or field name to find its source and relevant type. Keep secrets out of diagnostic output.

title: Key/value storage
Poster badges
Public settings
body:
Read current non-secret configuration for each request. No permission declaration is needed for your own public settings. Missing optional settings need a caller-selected default.

```ts
const count = Number(ether.settings.get().maxItems ?? 12);
```

The declarations and implementations below specify arguments, return types, defaults, permission checks, limits, and errors. SDK adapters translate raw hosted calls to portable clients. See [SDKs](/plugins/reference/sdk-typescript) and [Errors](/plugins/reference/troubleshooting).

title: Sealed secrets
HTTP requests
Catalogue lookup
body:
Requires catalog: read. Hosted search clamps invalid limits to 100; get accepts one title ID. SDK and raw global argument shapes differ: use the exact declarations below. Do not scan all titles to answer a single request.

```ts
const titles = ether.catalog.search("Arrival");
```

The declarations and implementations below specify arguments, return types, defaults, permission checks, limits, and errors. SDK adapters translate raw hosted calls to portable clients. See [SDKs](/plugins/reference/sdk-typescript) and [Errors](/plugins/reference/troubleshooting).

title: Original add-on relay
body:
Hosted drafts imported from a Stremio add-on can ask the original provider while its address stays sealed. It is available only with the draft relay context; ordinary plugins cannot choose arbitrary provider URLs through this service.

```ts
const response = ether.addon.get("/catalog/movie/top.json");
```

The declarations and implementations below specify arguments, return types, defaults, permission checks, limits, and errors. SDK adapters translate raw hosted calls to portable clients. See [SDKs](/plugins/reference/sdk-typescript) and [Errors](/plugins/reference/troubleshooting).

title: Viewers & watch state
body:
Live viewer grants determine identity, history, and write access. Use granted() before selecting a viewer. History is bounded (host maximum 200). Watch-state writes are journalled and forbidden in read-only tool calls. Never infer authorization from a cached viewer ID.

```ts
const viewers = ether.viewers.granted();
```

Declare `viewers.write_watch_state: "granted_viewers"` and grant each target viewer. Call `ether.viewers.setWatchState({viewerId, titleId, watched})` with an owned playable `pk:<pluginId>:<kind>:<externalId>` ref or a catalogue movie or episode ID. SDK clients also accept the three positional arguments.

Subscribe to `viewer.watch.scrobbled` for manual marks and playback completions or use `viewer.watch.watched` and `viewer.watch.unwatched` to include imported current state. Subscribe to `viewer.watch.progress` for resume checkpoints in `positionMs`. The writer receives no echo from its own writes. Request `viewers.identity: "granted_viewers"` to receive the viewer ID for granted viewers.

Payloads include `titleKey`, `watched`, `state` and `source`. Sources are `playback`, `manual`, `plugin` and `import`. The optional `surface` identifies the app or writing plugin. Only the owner receives its item's `itemRef`. Catalogue events carry available `tmdbId`, `tvdbId` and `imdbId`. For episodes these identify the series and are paired with `season` and `episode`.

SDK adapters translate raw hosted calls to portable clients. See [SDKs](/plugins/reference/sdk-typescript) and [Errors](/plugins/reference/troubleshooting).

title: Collections
body:
Requires collections: write. Writes are journalled and permission-checked on every call. Remote request bodies are capped at 2 MiB. Use stable collection identity for updates. Read-only tool calls cannot mutate state.

```ts
ether.collections.upsert({id: "weekly", name: "Weekly picks", ids: []});
```

The declarations and implementations below specify arguments, return types, defaults, permission checks, limits, and errors. SDK adapters translate raw hosted calls to portable clients. See [SDKs](/plugins/reference/sdk-typescript) and [Errors](/plugins/reference/troubleshooting).

title: Kind item storage & visibility
Screens pushes
body: `ether.screens.invalidate()` makes your open screens and surfaces read their sources again now; `ether.screens.putRecords([{type, id, value}])` (at most 100) sends new values for your records to open screens already showing them. Both need the `screens` capability, return `{streams}` (how many open streams heard them) and do nothing when nobody is watching. Remote plugins call `POST /ether/plugin-host/screens/invalidate` and `POST /ether/plugin-host/screens/records {records}`. Go: `ctx.InvalidateScreens()`, `ctx.PutScreenRecords(...)`; Python: `host.screens.invalidate()`, `host.screens.put_records(...)`.

title: Source discovery
body:
Requires kind_resolver and sources: search, search+check, acquire, or acquire+check. Search permits indexer discovery, debrid checks, release inspection, and on-demand usenet_check; acquire permits opening content; +check additionally permits background usenet_check in jobs and schedules within the owner's per-plugin daily allowance (default 20/UTC day, configurable under Sources › Indexers › Daily budgets, answering rate_limited with retryAfterSec/retryAt once spent; on-demand viewer calls never count against it and verdicts are shared with Ether's availability/Play cache for 15 min good / 30 min bad). On viewer or deadline-bounded requests, indexer_search is deadline-aware by default: Ether caps the wait to remaining time minus max(1.5 s, 35%) (unbounded/background jobs still wait up to the 30 s ceiling), returning arrived results while stragglers finish into Ether's search cache as status: "pending". Indexers that repeatedly time out or fail enter Ether's shared circuit-breaker backoff (2 min..30 min) and are skipped immediately with status: "skipped" and reason: "paused_backoff". Optional firstResults (with settleMs, default 250 ms), minResults, skipIndexers, onlyIndexers, and timeoutMs (capped at 30000 ms and any tighter deadline reserve) further tune fan-out latency, and the response envelope includes per-indexer status in indexers: [{indexerId, indexer, status, results?, ms, reason?, error?}] (omitted for other source query kinds). Cached debrid candidates report holding services in acquisition order via cachedBy: [{id, name}] (omitted when uncached; on debrid_acquire, the service that served it). Return a release source after choosing a candidate instead of downloading in the request handler. Torrent releases follow the owner's debrid setting (queueing uncached downloads and answering preparing / 503 Retry-After when Cached torrents only is off); set release.cachedOnly: true to opt out.

```ts
const { candidates, indexers } = ether.sources.resolve({
  kind: "indexer_search",
  query: "Example",
  firstResults: true,
  settleMs: 250,
  timeoutMs: 5000,
});
```

The declarations and implementations below specify arguments, return types, defaults, permission checks, limits, and errors. SDK adapters translate raw hosted calls to portable clients (`kinds.resolveSources` returns candidates; `kinds.resolveSourcesWithResult` returns `{ candidates, indexers }`). See [SDKs](/plugins/reference/sdk-typescript) and [Errors](/plugins/reference/troubleshooting).

### Request an NZB

Use `sources.resolve({kind: "nzb_request", nzbRef})` with an opaque indexer search reference, or supply `nzbIdentity: {indexerId, guid}`. The single candidate contains a parsed `files` list, `fileCount`, and a permanent vault `nzbRef` for a playback source’s `release.nzbRef`. Ether uses the vault before spending any indexer grab. Search mirrors stable references in the deprecated fields as `ether-nzb:<nzbRef>` and `ether-torrent:<torrentRef>` for older plugins. Direct plugin HTTP calls to configured indexers are refused. Background requests require the `+check` grant and use its daily allowance.

title: Library blob cache
Frontend stream tickets & visibility
Storage & folders
Language model (AI)
Media container probing
Owner notices
body:
Posts a console notice, limited to five per hour. It does not send through a notification-channel plugin. Read errors and avoid repeated notices on a playback or progress path.

```ts
ether.notify.owner("New recordings are ready");
```

The declarations and implementations below specify arguments, return types, defaults, permission checks, limits, and errors. SDK adapters translate raw hosted calls to portable clients. See [SDKs](/plugins/reference/sdk-typescript) and [Errors](/plugins/reference/troubleshooting).

title: Archive member reads
body:
Hosted and remote clients can keep large data in the host's existing library
blob cache, reading only the metadata or descriptor bytes the plugin itself must parse.
Big media (streams, ROMs, disc images, firmware downloads) never goes through
`cache.read`, `archive.open`, or `archive.read` — Ether streams cached blobs and archive
members directly to clients itself (for example via frontend `{ blob: { libraryKey, ref, memberIndex } }`
descriptors in `internal/plugins/frontend_blob.go` and `frontend.streamURL`); these calls
are strictly for bytes the plugin must parse:

```ts
const limits = await ctx.ether.runtime!.limits();
const readBudget = limits.readBytes ?? 8 * 1024 * 1024; // clamp(memoryBytes / 4, 8 MiB, 512 MiB)
const cached = await ctx.ether.http.fetchToCache!({
  url: "https://datasets.example/platform.zip",
  libraryKey: "pk-community-example-library-games", // this plugin's own library
  name: "platform.zip",
});
const members = await ctx.ether.archive!.list(cached.blob);

// Batch up to 4096 members per call within readBytes:
const xmlMembers = members.filter(m => !m.unsafe && m.name.endsWith(".xml") && m.size > 0);
let batch: Array<{ member: number; offset: number; length: number }> = [];
let batchBytes = 0;
for (const m of xmlMembers) {
  const length = Math.min(m.size, readBudget);
  if (batch.length === 4096 || batchBytes + length > readBudget) {
    const results = await ctx.ether.archive!.read(cached.blob, batch);
    // results: [{ index, member, size, body: Uint8Array }] in request order
    batch = [];
    batchBytes = 0;
  }
  batch.push({ member: m.index, offset: 0, length });
  batchBytes += length;
}
if (batch.length > 0) {
  await ctx.ether.archive!.read(cached.blob, batch);
}

const extracted = await ctx.ether.archive!.extract(cached.blob, xmlMembers[0]!.index);
// {ref: "blob:<sha256>", size, sha1, md5, crc32} streamed directly into the library cache
```

`http.fetchToCache({url, headers?, keepHeadersOnRedirect?, libraryKey, name, timeoutMs?, resume?})` performs a GET, streams
up to the owner download ceiling (8 GiB by default), further bounded by the library cache quota, into the plugin's own library cache, and returns
`{blob, size, crc32, md5, sha1, status}`. SHA-256 is the blob reference.
Digests cover the stored response bytes in one pass. Compare the digest with
trusted catalogue metadata before serving a verified download. Non-2xx responses,
network failures, size overflow and quota failures return errors; they do not
publish a truncated blob. Redirects recheck the live network grant and the
existing SSRF policy. The existing content capability, network host declaration
and library cache quota apply; no new permission is needed. `timeoutMs` defaults
to 10 minutes (also the ceiling on viewer and interactive request paths); in a
job (`/ether/job/*`), schedule, or background context, `timeoutMs` may extend up
to the calling job's remaining deadline. Pass `resume: true` to continue a
partial download with `Range: bytes=<cached>-` when the server supports ranges
and strong `ETag` / `Last-Modified` validators match (restarting cleanly from
byte 0 otherwise); partial blobs obey per-library cache quotas and disk safety
and only become readable cache blobs once complete. The operation is
synchronous; there is no background
prefetch. Cache eviction still applies to returned refs.

The per-call byte ceiling `readBytes` for `cache.read`, `archive.open`, and `archive.read`
scales with the plugin's granted memory: `readBytes = clamp(memoryBytes / 4, 8 MiB, 512 MiB)`
(default 32 MiB plugin memory → 8 MiB per call; declaring `runtime.limits.memoryBytes` of 1 GiB
grants 256 MiB per call). Plugins inspect their live grant via `runtime.limits`
(`ctx.ether.runtime!.limits()`, `BlobHost.RuntimeLimits`, `host.runtime.limits()`, or
`GET /ether/plugin-host/limits`) to size batches without guessing.

`cache.read(blob, {offset, length})` reads `1..readBytes` from a cached blob.
`archive.list(blob)` returns `[{index, name, size, unsafe?, unsafeReason?}]`, reading ZIP, 7z or RAR (4.x/5.x) headers
without loading all compressed bytes. `archive.open(blob, memberIndex, {offset, length})`
returns `1..readBytes` from one **uncompressed** member, while `archive.read(blob, reads)`
reads `1..4096` `{member, offset, length}` ranges in one call whose requested `length`s sum
to at most `readBytes` (returning an error rather than truncating when exceeded) and returns
`[{index, member, size, body}]` in request order (`bodyBase64` on raw JSON wire calls).
Use `archive.open` when reading one member or stepping sequentially through a single large
member across range calls. Use `archive.read` when parsing many small or medium members from
the same cached archive, amortizing cache ownership checks, directory lookup, and host crossings
into a single call. Offsets are nonnegative integers; a read at EOF returns empty bytes and reads
crossing EOF return the available suffix. Every call opens only the calling plugin's cache
namespace and closes every member stream and blob handle before returning.
`archive.extract(blob, memberIndex[, {libraryKey?, name?}])` streams the
uncompressed member directly into the plugin's own library blob cache (defaulting to
the source archive's library namespace) in one pass with no full in-memory buffer,
computing `{ref, size, sha1, md5, crc32}` (`ref` is `"blob:<sha256>"`). It enforces
`archiveMemberBytes` and the target library's cache quota, falls back to
`member-<index>` as the cache entry name when `options.name` is omitted for an unsafe
member name, refuses directories, observes cancellation and
deadlines, and charges governance units per started MiB (`ArchiveExtractUnitsPerMiB`).
The Go `RemoteHostClient` provides `RuntimeLimits`, `FetchToCache`, `CacheRead`, `ArchiveList`,
`ArchiveOpen`, `ArchiveRead`, and `ArchiveExtract` through `BlobHost`; the Python
`RemoteHostClient` and `MockHostClient` expose `runtime.limits()` and `archive.list`,
`archive.open`, `archive.read`, and `archive.extract`.

Archive sizes and member counts use owner global/per-plugin ceilings: defaults
are 8 GiB compressed archive/member, 32 GiB total expansion and 65,535 members.
Member names are limited to 1024 bytes. ZIP supports Store/Deflate and ZIP64;
7z supports Copy, LZMA and LZMA2 (including solid blocks); RAR supports stored
and compressed 4.x/5.x members. Other 7z coder chains are refused, including
BCJ filters and PPMd. Split/multi-volume input, encrypted headers or members,
links and other special files are refused. `archive.list` flags unsafe member
names with `unsafe: true` and `unsafeReason` as informational warnings (never
use stored names as filesystem paths), while `archive.open`, `archive.read`,
`archive.extract`, and frontend blob streaming open any non-directory member by
index. Directories may appear
in listings but cannot be opened. A 1000:1 expansion ceiling applies per ZIP
member and per 7z/RAR compression block. Nothing is extracted to a filesystem.

Metadata and decoder allocations are bounded by `memoryBytes` (32 MiB by
default). ZIP directories also retain the 64 MiB host ceiling. A large dictionary
or directory can be refused even when the member fits the byte grant. 7z uses
at most half the memory grant for its dictionary; RAR reserves one eighth per
decoder buffer, including PPMd and filters. Compressed input bytes read, including
metadata and decoder read-ahead, are cumulatively bounded by `fetchBytes` per
call. Expanded solid blocks and the whole declared expansion are bounded by
`archiveExpandedBytes`. Calls observe the runtime deadline and cancellation.

A range is a bound on **returned bytes**, not decompression work. Deflate reads
start at the member beginning. Solid 7z/RAR ranges decode dependencies from the
block beginning, then discard bytes through the requested offset. Calls are
stateless: sequential calls also restart decoding. RAR can additionally consume
earlier solid blocks in archive order. Prefer large sequential
chunks and avoid repeated random reads; persist verification digests in KV.
Range reads do not independently verify the full member CRC; use trusted digests
when integrity matters. Local owner-granted paths are not archive inputs: first
use a plugin-owned cached blob. Gzip files are unsupported here.
An HTTP `Content-Encoding: gzip` response may be transparently decoded by the
HTTP client; its digests then describe the decoded bytes. A `.gz` file is not
automatically decompressed by this archive service.

Direct `http.fetch` still limits the raw response to 10 MiB, with its JSON result
allowance including encoding expansion. Hosted WASM host-result envelopes also scale
automatically with the plugin's `readBytes` grant (including base64 and JSON framing
overhead, with a 4 MiB baseline floor), while hosted QuickJS binary reads transfer
decoded bytes directly into guest `ArrayBuffer`s. Big media never goes through these
read calls — Ether streams blobs and archive members itself (`internal/plugins/frontend_blob.go`).
